analysis: Reviewed GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift (test-only change). The diff adds a CryptoKit import, GLMMediaMarkerTokenizer (stub tokenizer with media special-token IDs), an openRouterVideo helper (reads fixtures via #filePath and verifies SHA-256), RequestCapture and PreparedCapture helpers, and the openRouterReadinessVideosReachTheEngineInsteadOfInvalidMedia test. The test routes real OpenRouter readiness clips (.mov and .mp4) through EngineV2VisionPlumbing, GLM5NextProcessor.prepareDetailed and the scheduler, using a scripted engine. It asserts that grid and span counts match, so a regression of the earlier invalid_media refusal would be caught. No production code, trust boundary, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache storage or coordinator/provider wire contract is modified, so none of the threat-model assets (A-001, A-003, A-008, A-015 to A-017) or boundaries (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011) are affected. The fixtures are local repository resources with pinned hashes, with no network access, secrets or temp-file writes. The test only reads fixtures, so it does not touch T-050 (inline video plaintext in temp files). Indirect relevance: the test exercises video ingest and decode paths (MediaIngest, GLM5NextProcessor), which are parts of the media-handling attack surface, and the test asserts that processor refusals remain client faults (HTTP 400) and that weight faults stay retriable. Behavior of the production sources (EngineV2VisionPrefill.glm5NextUserInput, glm5NextInputError, GLM5NextProcessor) was not supplied. Whether the underlying production changes introduce bounds or decoder issues (e.g., budget enforcement for the variable-frame-rate QuickTime path) cannot be judged from this test file and belongs to the other units of the PR.
